previews.title: 2026-27 Mid-American Men's Basketball Overview
previews.author: Kaily "KG" Godek and Foster Roesti
previews.summary: Team-by-team overview of all 12 MAC programs for 2026-27, organized by each team's preseason coaches-poll ranking rather than the authors' own projection. Notes that Northern Illinois has left, that four programs changed head coaches, that every team lost at least four players to the portal and added at least three, and that the league took in 64 transfers, 11 of them from Big Ten, Big East and Big 12 schools. Each section covers last season's record, returners, incoming transfers, notable losses and non-conference highlights. The piece states every team opens on the road against a Sun Belt opponent, though some listed openers (e.g., Toledo at Michigan State) do not match that.
notable_claims: Akron (29-6, 17-1 last season) returns Evan Mahaffey (10.2 PPG, 5.6 RPG, 3.4 APG, All-MAC HM, All-Defensive) and adds Ty Pence (Illinois State), Tahj Staveskie (Incarnate Word, 17.3 PPG) and Max Burton (Western Michigan); Akron has won three straight MAC tournaments.

Ball State (12-19) under new coach Chris Capko adds Javion Guy-King (Central Arkansas, 9.8 PPG), K'Jei Parker (UMass, 35.7% 3PT), Babatunde Durodola (Temple), Kijani Wright, Jaden Smith (Saint Joseph's) and Trey Lewis (Western Michigan); lost Preston Copeland to Miami and Armoni Ziegler to Boston College.

Bowling Green (18-14, 9-9) adds D-II shooters Zach Howell (Drury, 44% 3PT) and Trey Simmons (Frostburg State, 38%) plus Michigan Mr. Basketball KJ Torbert; lost Javontae Campbell (Cincinnati) and Mayar Wol (Seton Hall); allowed 71.6 PPG last season.

Buffalo (17-15, 7-11) has no returning starters and lost its top six scorers; adds J.J. Starling (Syracuse), Dylan Ducommun (Northern Illinois), Jalen Pitre (Tennessee Tech) and lower-division transfers.

Central Michigan (10-21) returns Phat Phat Brooks (11.0 PPG, 3.9 APG) and adds JUCO shooter Jayden Hackett (44.3% 3PT) and D-II rim protector Conrad Luczynski (2.3 BPG); non-conference includes Dayton, Pittsburgh, Notre Dame and Arkansas, called the MAC's toughest.

Eastern Michigan (10-21, 4-14) returns Mohammad Habhab (14.2 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 1.4 BPG, All-Freshman) under new coach Billy Donlon; adds Kaden Johnson (Huntington), Kilian Brockhoff (William & Mary), Emanuel Richards (Longwood), Jabri Fitzpatrick (New Haven); lost Godslove Nwabude to Kent State.
Kent State (24-10, 14-4) returns Quinn Woidke (9.0 PPG, All-Freshman) and adds Godslove Nwabude; lost Delrecco Gillespie (Houston), Cian Medley (East Carolina) and Jahari Williamson (Pepperdine).

UMass (16-16, 7-11) returns starters Jayden Ndjigue and Danny Carbuccia (6.3 APG, All-Freshman) and adds Jordan Clayton (Northwestern), Junjie 'Barry' Wang (San Francisco) and Abdullah Ahmed (BYU); 78.5% of last season's scoring departed; non-conference includes Boston College at TD Garden and Wake Forest.

Miami (OH) (32-2, 18-0) returns Evan Ipsaro, Luke Skaljac (All-MAC Third Team), Almar Atlason, Antwone Woolfolk (All-MAC HM) and Justin Kirby; adds Preston Copeland (Ball State), Rich Rolf (Youngstown State), Stevie Elam (Milwaukee) and freshmen Alan Horton, Anthony Fresh and Danny Kelly; lost MAC POY Peter Suder (graduated), Brant Byers (Penn State), Eian Elmer (Wisconsin), Trey Perry (Coastal Carolina).

Ohio (15-17, 9-9) returns Jackson Paveletzke (All-MAC Second Team, 17.3 PPG, 5.3 APG) and Javan Simmons; adds Kyler D'Augustino (IU Indy, All-Horizon Third Team), Moek Icke (Rhode Island) and Che Brogan (Australia); lost JJ Kelly to UTSA; Ohio is one of only three MAC teams returning an All-MAC player.

Toledo returns Austin Parks (10.7 PPG, 7.3 RPG, 44 blocks), Jaylan Ouwinga and Mynor Strong and adds Angel Montas Jr. (UMass Lowell, 15.8 PPG, America East First Team); lost MAC Freshman of the Year Leroy Blyden Jr. (Kansas) and All-MAC Second Teamer Sonny Wilson (South Florida); plays Michigan State Nov. 5 and Michigan Dec. 30; last MAC tournament title was 1980.

Western Michigan under new coach Kahil Fennell has no returning players; adds Isaac Finlinson (Hawaii, 39.1% 3PT), Rob Lee Jr. (Lamar, 16.0 PPG) and 6-11 German freshman Janis Junemann; lost Max Burton (Akron), Trey Lewis (Ball State), Jalen Griffith (Eastern Washington), Carson Vis (Northern Iowa).

previews.outlet: The Eastern Echo (Eastern Michigan student paper)
previews.title: 2026-27 MAC Men's basketball season preview
previews.author: Ruby Brannon
previews.summary: EMU-centered preview of the 2026-27 season under new head coach Billy Donlon, who the article says was appointed in April 2026 after stints as head coach at Wright State and Kansas City and as a top assistant at Clemson. The Eagles are anchored by First-Team Preseason All-MAC forward Mohammad Habhab, who entered the transfer portal during the coaching change but returned after talks with Donlon. Non-conference schedule includes an exhibition at defending national champion Michigan, the MAC/Sun Belt Challenge opener at Coastal Carolina, the Cancun Tournament, and road games at Louisville and Xavier. League context places Miami, Ball State, Toledo and Akron as top-tier contenders in preseason polling with EMU in the middle pack, and notes the MAC Tournament is revising its seeding to reward regular-season performance.
notable_claims: Billy Donlon was named Eastern Michigan head coach in April 2026 (note: Wikipedia and mlive date the hire to March 17, 2026).
Mohammad Habhab entered the transfer portal during the coaching transition but returned to EMU; the article describes him as able to guard positions 1-5 and facilitate from the high post.
Emanuel Richards led EMU in scoring on a three-game Canadian summer tour; Braelon Green is a returning guard who had a strong summer.
EMU's non-conference slate includes Coastal Carolina (MAC-SBC Challenge), Kennesaw State and either College of Charleston or UTEP in Cancun, Louisville, Xavier, Detroit Mercy and Denver.
Donlon's stated off-court goal is the program's first-ever men's basketball sellout at the George Gervin GameAbove Center.
The article describes Miami, Ball State, Toledo and Akron as top-tier in preseason polling (note: Ball State was actually picked 11th in the official coaches poll).

previews.title: Cooper's Corner: What are fair expectations for the men's basketball 2026-27 season?
previews.author: Cooper Meneghetti
previews.summary: Column arguing Miami (OH) can contend for a top-four MAC finish despite post-Cinderella turnover. Travis Steele stayed after outside interest and signed an eight-year extension; Peter Suder graduated and went to the NBA, Eian Elmer and Brant Byers transferred, and Antwone Woolfolk's status depends on an eligibility court case. Returning guards Luke Skaljac and Evan Ipsaro (back from a season-ending injury) lead, with transfers Stevie Elam (Milwaukee), Preston Copeland (Ball State) and Rich Rolf (Youngstown State) added. The author projects at least 27 wins if healthy and flags Dec. 12 at High Point and a Jan. 5-16 stretch (at Toledo, at Akron, vs. Western Michigan, at Kent State) as the likeliest losses.
notable_claims: Travis Steele signed an eight-year contract extension with Miami (OH).
Antwone Woolfolk's availability depends on an eligibility court case.
Stevie Elam (sophomore guard, from UW-Milwaukee) is projected as Miami's third double-digit scorer.
Justin Kirby (sophomore guard/wing) is expected to take a big step after breaking out late last season.
Miami opens at James Madison and plays at High Point on Dec. 12.
Author projects a top-four MAC seed at minimum and at least 27 wins if the core stays healthy; names Toledo, Akron, Western Michigan and Kent State as title rivals.

previews.title: Miami RedHawks open as MAC favorites; two guards land preseason honors
previews.author: WKRC staff
previews.summary: News report on the MAC preseason coaches poll. Miami (OH) was picked first with 130 points and 9 of 12 first-place votes, Toledo second with 2 first-place votes, and Kent State received the remaining first-place vote; Miami also got 5 of 12 votes to win the MAC Tournament. Evan Ipsaro and Luke Skaljac were named Preseason All-MAC First Team. Miami returns 11 players from a 32-win team that went undefeated in the 2025-26 regular season and won a First Four game, its first NCAA Tournament win since 1999; Travis Steele enters his fifth season and captains are Ipsaro, Skaljac and Almar Atlason.
notable_claims: Miami (OH) returns 11 players from the 2025-26 roster.
Team captains for 2026-27 are Evan Ipsaro, Luke Skaljac and Almar Atlason.
Miami won a program-record 32 games in 2025-26 and its first NCAA Tournament game since 1999 (First Four).

storylines.headline: Northern Illinois departs; MAC plays as a 12-team league with a full 22-game double round-robin
storylines.detail: NIU left for the Horizon League effective July 1, 2026, the first MAC season without NIU since 1996-97. The 2026-27 schedule has every team playing every other team home and away (22 games, 11 home/11 away) over 12 weeks, starting Wednesday Dec. 2, 2026 and ending Friday March 5, 2027. Wikipedia's season page describes this as the first season with a balanced round-robin.

storylines.headline: Four new head coaches: Akron, Ball State, Eastern Michigan, Western Michigan
storylines.detail: Akron: John Groce left for College of Charleston (Mar 30, 2026); associate HC Dustin Ford promoted. Ball State: fired Michael Lewis (Mar 7, 2026; 61-64 in four seasons) and hired SMU associate HC Chris Capko. Eastern Michigan: parted with Stan Heath (Mar 8, 2026; 57-99 in five seasons) and hired Clemson associate HC Billy Donlon (Mar 17, 2026). Western Michigan: fired Dwayne Stephens (Mar 10, 2026; 42-84 in four seasons) and hired UTRGV coach Kahil Fennell (Mar 23, 2026; 35-29 at UTRGV).

storylines.headline: Miami (OH) favored to repeat after 32-2, 18-0 season; loses MAC POY Peter Suder
storylines.detail: Miami took 9 of 12 first-place votes and 5 of 12 tournament-champion votes in the coaches poll and is picked to win its first MAC Tournament since 2007. Suder graduated (went to the NBA per The Miami Student), Brant Byers (Penn State) and Eian Elmer (Wisconsin) transferred; Evan Ipsaro and Luke Skaljac return as Preseason All-MAC First Teamers alongside transfers Preston Copeland, Rich Rolf and Stevie Elam. Travis Steele signed an eight-year extension.

storylines.headline: Heavy transfer-portal churn across the league
storylines.detail: sMACk Talk counted 64 incoming transfers league-wide, 11 from Big Ten/Big East/Big 12 programs, with every team losing at least four players and adding at least three. Notable outbound: Leroy Blyden Jr. (Toledo to Kansas), Sonny Wilson (Toledo to South Florida), Delrecco Gillespie (Kent State to Houston), Tavari Johnson (Akron), Javontae Campbell (BG to Cincinnati). Notable inbound: J.J. Starling (Syracuse to Buffalo), Jordan Clayton (Northwestern to UMass), Angel Montas Jr. (UMass Lowell to Toledo), Tahj Staveskie (Incarnate Word to Akron). Western Michigan and Buffalo return no starters.

storylines.headline: Revised 2027 MAC Tournament format: eight teams, double byes for top two seeds
storylines.detail: The MAC announced (Aug 12-13, 2026) a revised format for the 2027 men's and women's tournaments: the top eight teams qualify, the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds receive byes into the semifinals, and the No. 3 and No. 4 seeds receive byes into the quarterfinals. The men's tournament runs March 10-13, 2027 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, its 28th consecutive year there (contract through 2030). The tournament champion receives the automatic NCAA bid.

storylines.headline: MAC-Sun Belt Challenge continues; all 12 teams open the season against SBC opponents
storylines.detail: The 2026-27 MAC-SBC Challenge opened the season in early November with MAC teams on the road, and the return round on Saturday Feb. 6, 2027 has all MAC men's teams hosting Sun Belt opponents. Pairings were announced June 29 / July 1-2, 2026.

storylines.headline: TV: MAC 2026-27 broadcast schedule released mid-October on ESPN platforms and CBS Sports Network
storylines.detail: Per an Akron Athletics release republished Oct 14, 2026, the MAC announced its 2026-27 men's basketball broadcast schedule with national games on ESPN platforms and CBS Sports Network and a 21-day wildcard selection process for additional national slots; Akron has three confirmed national TV games including two vs. Miami (OH) and at Toledo on Friday Jan. 15. The league office had said in August the full TV schedule would come in October. A MAC Men's and Women's Basketball Tip-Off show aired Oct 20, 2026 on Field of 68, with each head coach and two student-athletes per school interviewed. The full league-wide national TV release on getsomemaction.com was not located.

storylines.headline: UMass enters its second MAC season touting a deeper roster
storylines.detail: Frank Martin (fifth season) returns Jayden Ndjigue and Danny Carbuccia and added Jordan Clayton (Northwestern), Barry Wang (San Francisco) and Abdullah Ahmed (BYU); the Minutemen were picked sixth and received 2 of 12 tournament-champion votes. Regional coverage (Athol Daily News, Aug 4, 2026) quoted Martin calling it his most complete team; UMass plays Boston College at TD Garden and Wake Forest in the Hall of Fame Classic.
